Scree plot of a PCAtools pca object

Source: R/pcaPlots.R
pcaScreePlot.Rd

The interactive counterpart of PCAtools::screeplot(): the percentage of variance each component explains, with the cumulative percentage as a line. The elbow of the curve (PCAtools::findElbowPoint(), when PCAtools is installed) and any other components you choose (e.g. the number retained by PCAtools::parallelPCA(), which needs the original data matrix) can be marked with vertical lines.

Usage

pcaScreePlot(
  pcaobj,
  components = NULL,
  show.cumulative = TRUE,
  show.elbow = TRUE,
  mark.components = NULL,
  bar.color = "#1E90FF",
  line.color = "#CD2626",
  main = NULL
)

Arguments

pcaobj

A PCAtools pca object.

components

Components to show, by name. Default: the first 20.

show.cumulative

Logical; draw the cumulative percentage line.

show.elbow

Logical; mark the elbow component.

mark.components

Integer indices of further components to mark.

bar.color, line.color

Colours of the bars and the cumulative line.

main

Optional plot title.

Value

A plotly object. The table it draws is attached as attribute "table".

See also

pcaScreePlotServer(), PCAtools::screeplot()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

data(example_pca)
pcaScreePlot(example_pca)
